kernels.l1: Half a cookie is a real amount. Pieces are numbers too.
kernels.l2: When sharing does not come out whole, the answer is a piece of a whole — a fraction. Adding and multiplying fractions always gives you another fraction.
kernels.l3: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing fractions always gives another fraction, as long as you never divide by zero. The reciprocal is exactly what the whole numbers were missing.
kernels.l4: ℚ is closed under addition, additive inverses, multiplication, and multiplicative inverses of nonzero elements — this makes ℚ a field. A ring lacks the last property; a field has it.
kernels.l5: ℚ satisfies every ring axiom plus the existence of multiplicative inverses for nonzero elements, which is what a field is; ℤ is a ring but not a field.
kernels.l6: ℚ is closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by anything nonzero — the four operations that make it a field. ℤ fails the last one, having no reciprocals. Every closure proof is fraction arithmetic checked against the definition.
kernels.l7: ℚ is closed under all four field operations, with division defined for nonzero denominators, so ℚ is a field; the proofs are the standard fraction formulas read as closure statements.
kernels.l8: ℚ is the field of fractions of ℤ, the smallest field containing it; finite fields ℤ/pℤ show that fields need not be infinite, and characteristic distinguishes them.
